To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have obtained mouse monoclonal antibodies which are highly specific for human breast cancer cells and can be used in vitro and in a model of in vivo invasiveness of these cells.
we have developed a panel of mouse monoclonal antibodies that recognize a set of antigens expressed on epithelial cells and that can be used in immunohistochemical analysis.
we have developed a set of monoclonal antibodies that recognize antigens expressed by epithelial cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the production of Mabs against human breast cancer cell lines, with the characterization of their specificity, and the use of one of them as a tool to study tumor invasiveness in vitro and in a nude mouse model.
the production of Mabs against human breast cancer, with the study of the specificity of the Mabs obtained, and with the development of an in vitro and an in vivo model of breast cancer invasion.
the production and characterization of a panel of Mabs raised against MCF-7 human breast cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these Mabs are of great value in the characterization and study of human breast cancer.

the monoclonal anti-epithelium antibodies are useful in immunohistochemical studies for the detection of epithelial cells, both in normal and neoplastic tissues, and in the in vitro study of invasiveness.

MCF-7 cell lines have a high immunogenic potential.
the Mabs developed are of potential interest for the immunohistochemical diagnosis of human breast cancer.

the use of monoclonal antibodies in the study of breast cancer is feasible, and that the use of a human tumor cell line as the immunogen is a valid approach.
